items.claim: The dated siege notice, breach notice, and officers'-entry report are correctly held as one unit, with both boundaries carried by disclosed apparatus and a clean subject-shift seam into the next unit.
items.evidence: The setumah at Jer.39.1 and the doubled setumah-and-petuchah closing the preceding unit at Jer.38.28 both match the marked-verse inventory exactly. The verse-initial date frames at 39:1 (bishnat) and 39:2 (a bet-prefixed cardinal) are correctly read as their own distinct constructions rather than folded into any of the book's three counted word-event shapes, none of which include 39:1. No paseq or ketiv/qere note exists inside this span per the same inventory, so nothing is omitted. The back seam at Jer.39.3|Jer.39.4 (a general entry report giving way to Zedekiah personally) is independently confirmed by the immediately following unit's own opening warrant.

items.claim: The paseq at Jer.39.4 is disclosed correctly, and this unit properly treats the Zedekiah capture-and-sentencing report's recurrence in the closing appendix as non-driving narrative texture rather than boundary evidence.
items.evidence: The marked-verse inventory confirms a paseq at 39:4 exactly where disclosed (single-witness, count-only), and the resh-family Nebuchadnezzar spelling cited at 39:5 matches the name inventory. The device note that this span's report 'recurs with variation later in the book at the corresponding point of the closing appendix' and 'plays no part in the boundary argued above' correctly applies the ruled typed-relation treatment to the synoptic overlap without using it as evidence. Both boundaries are independently carried: the front seam matches the preceding unit's own close, and the back seam (king personally to the city) is confirmed by the following unit's own opening warrant.

items.claim: This unit's content sits inside the same flagged narrative-overlap block as the immediately preceding unit but, unlike that unit, discloses no relationship to the closing appendix's parallel account of the same events.
items.evidence: The immediately preceding unit (Jer.39.4-Jer.39.7) explicitly discloses that its own report of Zedekiah's capture 'recurs with variation later in the book at the corresponding point of the closing appendix,' naming the relationship as non-driving narrative texture. This unit reports the burning of the city, the deportation, and the provision made for the poor left behind - content reported a second time at that same later point in the book exactly as the preceding unit's episode is - yet carries no equivalent disclosure anywhere in its own prose. No apparatus mark (petuchah/setumah, paseq, or ketiv/qere) exists inside this span to compensate for the gap; the omission is specifically the appendix-relationship disclosure that the immediately adjoining unit supplies for its own, adjacent portion of the same flagged span.
tier_citations: cross-tradition/synoptic-relation disclosure practice, typed-relation metadata class

items.claim: The small nun at Jer.39.13 and the setumah at Jer.39.14 are disclosed correctly, but a ketiv/qere note at Jer.39.12, inside this same unit's own span, goes completely undisclosed.
items.evidence: The marked-verse inventory confirms exactly one special-letter seg in the whole book, the x-small nun at 39:13 as disclosed, and a setumah at 39:14 as disclosed. The same inventory also carries a ketiv/qere note at 39:12, squarely inside this unit's four-verse span; the unit's own prose moves directly from the command's opening at verse 11 to the officer roster at verse 13 without engaging verse 12's content or citing it individually anywhere (verse 12 appears only inside the outer range citation), so its apparatus note receives no disclosure at all. The two neighboring apparatus classes in this same short span are handled correctly, which makes the missing one a clean omission rather than a general disclosure weakness.

items.claim: This unit's own quotation of verse 18 renders two of the source text's internal closing marks as straight typewriter punctuation rather than the curly marks the WEB text itself carries, and the resumptive, pre-siege-fall timing of verse 15's own content goes undrawn.
items.evidence: This unit's quotation of verse 18 closes with three punctuation marks in sequence: one closing the embedded 'Behold...' clause after 'trust in me,', one closing the 'Yahweh of Armies...' clause after 'Yahweh', and one closing the unit's own outer quotation. In the unit's own stored text, the first two of these are plain straight-typewriter marks (a straight double quote and a straight apostrophe) rather than the curly marks the staged WEB text carries at both positions; only the third, outermost mark is curly. The same unit discloses the ketiv/qere note at 39:16 correctly, so the mismatch is specific to this one nested quotation. Separately, verse 15 reports Yahweh's word coming to Jeremiah 'while he was shut up in the court of the guard' - a state prior to the siege's fall - so this unit reports an episode set before, not after, the custody transfer just narrated in the immediately preceding unit; the clause is quoted but the unit never states that it resumes an earlier moment rather than continuing the narrative forward.
tier_citations: byte tier: unit's own stored characters vs. staged WEB verse text

items.claim: The header-shape-deviation argument at Jer.40.1 is well-grounded and correctly typed, but two of this unit's WEB quotations render the source text's own internal marks as straight punctuation, and a paseq at Jer.40.1 inside the unit's own span goes undisclosed.
items.evidence: The disclosure that the hadavar-shaped header at 40:1 frames a release narrative rather than a sermon, with unit_type correctly set to narrative rather than mechanically inherited from the header's formal shape, is accurate and well reasoned. However, this unit's own quotation of verse 2 opens 'Yahweh your God pronounced this evil...' with a straight double quote where the staged WEB text carries a curly opening mark, and its quotation of verse 4 closes '...go there.' with a straight double quote immediately before its own, correctly curly, outer close, again where the source carries a curly mark at that inner position. Separately, the marked-verse inventory carries a paseq at 40:1, inside this unit's own span, that is never mentioned, even though the same unit correctly discloses the ketiv/qere note at 40:3 and the preceding unit's closing setumah at 39:18.
tier_citations: byte tier: unit's own stored characters vs. staged WEB verse text

items.claim: The single-verse relocation notice is correctly isolated from the administrative narrative that the ruled architecture begins at the following verse, with its own apparatus disclosed and its genuine uncertainty honestly calibrated.
items.evidence: The setumah at 40:6 matches the marked-verse inventory exactly, and the short-spelling Gedaliah count ("sweep: 4 verses") matches the name inventory's site list exactly, including the contrasting long-form citation at 40:9. This unit's medium_low confidence and frontier flag are well calibrated: it explicitly declines to force a choice between folding this verse backward into the release scene or forward into the captains' arrival, leaving that question open rather than argued past its evidence. No WEB quotation in this unit shows a mark-fidelity defect.

items.claim: This unit discloses the ketiv/qere note and one paseq at Jer.40.8 correctly, but a separate paseq at Jer.40.7 inside the same span is not mentioned, and its quotation of verse 9 opens an embedded speech with a straight mark where the source carries a curly one.
items.evidence: The marked-verse inventory confirms a ketiv/qere note and a paseq both at 40:8, which this unit discloses together, and a setumah at 40:6 (the preceding unit's close), also disclosed. The same inventory carries a further, separate paseq at 40:7, inside this unit's own span, that receives no mention; the unit's own device note describes the apparatus as converging "at" verse 8 alone, which leaves the verse-7 paseq unaccounted for rather than merely uncounted. Separately, this unit's quotation of verse 9 renders Gedaliah's sworn assurance as opening with a straight double quote before 'Don't be afraid to serve the Chaldeans,' where the staged WEB text itself opens that embedded speech with a curly mark, unbalanced against the unit's own correctly curly outer quotation marks.
tier_citations: byte tier: unit's own stored characters vs. staged WEB verse text
